order_reconstruction_rule.rule: GROUP BY (user_id, user_session, event_time) on event_type='purchase' rows
order_reconstruction_rule.certified_because: 98.1% of multi-purchase-row sessions share one identical purchase timestamp across all their purchase rows; session-only grouping (Rule A) produces implausible order spans (max observed ~full dataset window) due to session-ID reuse documented in Section 7.
order_reconstruction_rule.rejected_alternative: one order per user_session (ignores possible multiple checkout events within one reused/long-lived session id)

retention_horizon.primary_reason: Only horizon with a full-cohort-trustworthy trailing window for nearly the entire dataset (Oct/Nov/Dec cohorts fully covered, Jan cohort nearly covered).

churn_threshold_candidates_days.note: Candidates only -- nb03 must still validate FP rate and recall against future behavior.

superseded.reason_superseded: Pooling weights frequent repeat-buyers more heavily, biasing every percentile down by roughly 15-20%. Kept here only for audit trail.

nb03_status.median_22.0: validated, rejected (J too low, flags 77% of the base)
nb03_status.p95_87.3: NOT VALIDATABLE -- dropped on window arithmetic, never scored

known_limitations: user_id is cookie-scoped, not account-scoped -- every repeat-purchase/retention figure is a LOWER BOUND on true customer-level behavior.
category_code is null for ~98% of events -- use category_id for category-level grouping.
brand is null for ~42% of events.

Bot exclusion IS defined and applied project-wide since 01: sessions per active day (distinct user_session count / distinct active-day count) > 29.0 (1,605 users, 1.743% of events). Inherit it from handoff_params.json bot_exclusion; do not re-derive.

The order-size tail is NOT bot-driven (00's claim, disproved in 01) and is not an anomaly: 143 reseller/B2B-like bulk buyers (median ~130 distinct products over ~31 categories at a BELOW-average unit price). Kept and flagged as is_bulk_buyer in data/processed/cohort_assignments.parquet; exclude from MEAN-based monetary metrics in 04/05, report medians as headline.

DuckDB determinism: never reference row_number() OVER () through a lazy view (it is re-assigned per reference and corrupts joins -- this silently broke 01's first two commits), and never use approx_quantile for a reported figure. See src/data.py connect().
01's 4-type cart-abandonment decomposition is partial: 02 Section 0A splits the 48% residual, promoting `substitution` to a named type and leaving only `returned_browsed_only` unclassified.

OUTCOME LEAKAGE: the abandonment-type ranking in 01 Section 4 and 02 Section 0A is NOT a valid effect size -- the types' definitions reference purchases that can fall in the outcome window. 02 Section 0E re-tests with disjoint windows: deferred_intent collapses from OR 10.81 to 0.78 and the ranking inverts. Only abandonment VOLUME survives. nb05 must not build features from those types -- see leakage_rules_for_05.
The 'promo' cohort is a BLACK FRIDAY cohort: all detected discount-spike days fall in one week, so promo-vs-organic results are about a single trading event, not about discounting in general.

SPINE-1 FALSIFIED: behaviour (first-session depth) does NOT beat first-order value for predicting repeat purchase (D30 dead heat, value ahead at D60/D90) and both are weak (V~0.09-0.13). See spine_hypothesis_status; CLAUDE.md's spine has been revised accordingly.

CHURN THRESHOLD CERTIFIED: 42.2 days of purchase silence (P75 of per-user-median inter-purchase gaps), validated at flag date 2020-01-04 with FP rate 10.12% and recall 53.09% (Spec B). Inherit it from handoff_params.json churn_definition; do not re-derive or round it.
P95 CHURN CANDIDATE (87.3d) WAS NEVER TESTED and must not be cited as validated: it needs 2K=174.6 days of span against 152.0 available, so zero users can be scored against it.

D30 CANNOT MEASURE CHURN: under the certified 42.2d rule no user is churned before day 42.2, so 06's repeat_purchase_30d target is a REPEAT-PURCHASE target and must never be labelled churn. The shortest horizon that can carry a churn label is D43.

CHURN-THRESHOLD FLAG-DATE INSTABILITY: the J-optimal threshold drifts 43.5d -> 29.4d as the flag date moves 21 days earlier, tracking the shrinking lookback cap (95.1d -> 74.1d). This is left censoring in a 5-month window, not behaviour. Treat 42.2d as the centre of a 30-45d region; ~9 months of history would settle it.

ABANDONMENT-VOLUME SIGNAL IS ANCHOR-SENSITIVE: log1p(n_removals) holds at OR 1.37-1.44 for first-order-anchored outcomes at every churn threshold, but falls to 1.03-1.14 for a calendar-anchored churn label. 05 must carry time-since-first-order alongside it rather than expecting OR=1.38.

CHURN IS FIRST-PURCHASE CHURN: 88% of users flagged by the certified rule had exactly one order, vs 80% of the base. 04's at-risk cells and 08's intervention are activation problems (get a 2nd order), not win-back problems.

CHURN BASE RATE IS NOT RETENTION: 03's 84.84% true-churn base is a point-in-time STOCK measure on a calendar anchor; 02's 21.08% D60 retention is a FLOW measure anchored on each user's first order. Both are correct and they must never be quoted against each other. 03 Section 9A reproduces 02 exactly on the same users once the anchor is matched.

CHURN RULE RECALL IS 53%: the certified rule flags 36,495 users but the true at-risk base is 61,787. 08/09 must NOT treat flagged-population as at-risk-population -- every reach or ROI denominator built on the flagged count must be divided by recall (53.09%). All 28,986 missed churners sit BELOW the 42.2d threshold (median recency 23.7d).

CHURN THRESHOLD IS NOT IDENTIFIED: 42.2d is the centre of a 30-45d region; two independent methods agree there, but the estimate is robust to neither flag-date position nor cost asymmetry. ~9 months of history would identify it. Quote certified_region_days [30, 45], not the decimal; use 42.2d as the OPERATING value so 04/05/06 stay comparable.

bot_exclusion.metric: sessions per active day (distinct user_session count / distinct active-day count)
bot_exclusion.threshold_derivation: exact 99.9th percentile of the real distribution across all users; a generic Tukey far-outlier fence on raw session count was tested and rejected for over-flagging ordinary repeat shoppers (see notebook).
bot_exclusion.order_size_tail_correction: 00 claimed the order-size heavy tail was driven by the same high-volume user_ids; verified false -- zero overlap between the session-frequency bot list and the top mega-basket-order users, and the tail (max=429 items) is unchanged after bot exclusion. Treat as a separate, unresolved data issue for nb04/nb05.

bulk_buyer_segment.threshold_derivation: exact P99.9 of order size (quantile_cont), bot-excluded
bulk_buyer_segment.treatment: KEEP and flag as a named segment (is_bulk_buyer). Exclude from MEAN-based monetary metrics in 04/05 (AOV, mean CLV); report medians/winsorised means as headline.
bulk_buyer_segment.evidence: reseller/B2B signature: broad assortment, high volume, below-average unit price, one large haul, ~2x repeat rate of typical purchasers

retention_measured.definition_purchase: share of cohort placing >=1 further order within x days, in a session other than the first-order session
retention_measured.definition_activity: same window and session rule, any event type (superset of purchase)
retention_measured.eligibility_rule: cohort contributes to Dx only if its LAST joiner has >=x trailing days; ineligible cohorts are excluded, never zero-filled

compounding_vs_selection.implication_for_08: Do not assume an engineered 2nd purchase inherits the ~2x repeat rate; plan on the residual (1.27x), which is the part not explained by which buyers self-select into a fast 2nd purchase.

black_friday_cohort.naming_note: Renamed from 'promo_acquisition'. All detected spike days fall inside a single week, so this flag identifies the Black Friday cohort, not promotional acquisition generally. The old name overclaimed.
black_friday_cohort.spike_rule: day-level mean discount vs per-product median price exceeding median + 3*MAD of the daily series (derived from price dispersion only, no calendar input)
black_friday_cohort.primary_population: cohorts eligible at D90 (Oct+Nov), held fixed across D7..D90
black_friday_cohort.interpretation_limit: Associational, and about ONE trading week. Confounded with calendar position, merchandising and deal-seeking intent. Cannot justify a discounting decision on its own -- see 07 (Criteo) for randomised incrementality.

leakage_rules_for_05.rule: No feature may be derived from a cart-abandonment type whose definition references the outcome window. The 01/02 types (deferred_intent, substitution) require a purchase, and if that purchase is unbounded in time it can BE the predicted repeat purchase.
leakage_rules_for_05.evidence: Under the leaky spec deferred_intent scored OR=10.81 [10.29, 11.36]; with the classification window confined to events before the first order and the outcome measured strictly after it, the same type scores OR=0.78 [0.71, 0.85] -- below the baseline. The ranking inverts.
leakage_rules_for_05.safe_construction: Classify on events strictly before the first order (or a fixed first-k-day window); measure the outcome strictly after it; ensure every purchase a type definition references falls inside the classification window.
leakage_rules_for_05.what_survives: Abandonment VOLUME (log1p n_removals) remains predictive: OR=1.38 [1.35, 1.41]. Type does not.

spine_hypothesis_status.finding_name: SPINE-1: first-order value vs first-session depth is a dead heat, and both are weak
spine_hypothesis_status.original_claim: Repeat purchase is driven more by user behaviour and category/journey characteristics than by simple first-order value.
spine_hypothesis_status.verdict: First-order VALUE matches depth at D30 and exceeds it at D60 and D90. Behaviour does not beat first-order value. Both associations are weak (Cramer's V ~ 0.09-0.13), so neither is a strong standalone predictor of repeat purchase.
spine_hypothesis_status.replacement_framing: Repeat purchase and repeat engagement are separable problems at this retailer: by D90, 60% of purchasers return but only 27% buy again, a 33pp gap stable from D14 onward. Neither first-order value nor first-session depth predicts repeat purchase strongly, so the targeting question cannot be answered by propensity alone -- it requires estimating who would RESPOND to an intervention, which observational data cannot do (07/08).
spine_hypothesis_status.recorded_not_deleted: Kept as a named, dated falsification so 06/08 cannot silently re-adopt the original spine.

churn_definition.rule: A user is churned as of date D if (D - last order timestamp) >= 42.2 days, in exact elapsed seconds, over bot-excluded orders built with the certified order-reconstruction rule.

derivation.forward_method: max-separation cut (Youden's J) against a 56.9d forward window = 43.5d
derivation.why_this_is_the_certification: Two methods sharing no inputs land 1.3 days apart, and P75 scores J=19.63 against a ceiling of 19.90 -- it is on the plateau, not a slope.

churn_definition.reasoning: Certified on prevalence-free separation (Youden's J), NOT on misclassification cost. A cost sweep is degenerate here: at an 85% true-churn base rate, cost = c_FP*FP + c_FN*FN is minimised at K -> 0 for every R >= 0.47 and is strictly increasing in K from R >= 1.30, so across the whole economically sensible range it advises flagging everyone. Charging contact cost on all flagged users removes the degeneracy but breaks even between R=1.2 and 1.3, which nothing in the data pins down. Certifying a definition on intervention economics would make the churn rate a function of the marketing budget; the contact threshold is a separate decision and belongs in 08/09.
churn_definition.business_asymmetry_assumed: Symmetric per head: one missed churner costs about what one wasted contact costs (w=0.5). P75 wins only for w in [0.475, 0.525]; below that P85 wins, above it the 30-day rule and then the median win. The threshold is NOT robust to this assumption.

candidates_rejected.p95_87.3d: NOT VALIDATABLE. Needs 2K=174.6d of span; there are 152.0d. Its anchor falls 22 days before the first row of data, so zero users can be scored. Dropped, not weakly validated.
candidates_rejected.median_22d: J=13.72, flags 77% of the base -- close to flagging everyone.

naive_30d_contrast.direction: recency rules nest: the naive 30d rule flags a strict SUPERSET, 12,618 extra users, all with recency in [30, 42.2) days
naive_30d_contrast.honest_read: 30 days is a defensible operating point, not a catastrophic one -- 83% of its marginal contacts land on real churners. What deriving buys is a KNOWN position on the curve (J 17.02 vs 19.63 vs a ceiling of 19.90) and a priceable trade.

sensitivity_of_01_02_headlines.verdict: No conclusion from 01 or 02 reverses at any validatable threshold.
sensitivity_of_01_02_headlines.black_friday_gap: sign negative and CI excludes 0 in every measurable cell (range -7.83 to -2.46 pp); the 'WIDENS' trajectory is NOT assessable under P75/P85 because D7-D30 are unmeasurable
sensitivity_of_01_02_headlines.removal_volume_OR: first-order-anchored 1.37-1.44 at every K (02 committed 1.38); re-anchored to a calendar date it collapses to 1.03-1.14

persisted.labelled_panel: in_validation_panel == True (72,827 users) carries flagged_churned + true_churn_label

identification_status.claim: 42.2d is the centre of a 30-45d region; two independent methods agree there, but the estimate is robust to neither flag-date position nor cost asymmetry. ~9 months of history would identify it.
identification_status.why_an_operating_value_is_still_required: 04/05/06 must cut at one number or their results are not comparable. 42.2d is the best-supported point in the region; the region, not the decimal, is what the data supports.

evidence_against_precision.flag_date_drift: J-optimal K moves 43.5d -> 29.4d over 21 days of flag-date shift, tracking the lookback cap 95.1d -> 74.1d monotonically (Section 3D).
evidence_against_precision.cost_asymmetry_band: P75 wins only for recall weight w in [0.475, 0.525]; outside it P85 or the 30-day rule wins (Section 3C).
evidence_against_precision.taken_together: The estimate is robust to neither of the procedure's two free choices, so it is the value those choices produced rather than a property of the customers.

identification_status.what_survives: Every method tried lands in 30-45d (P75 42.2, forward-optimum at full lookback 43.5, forward-optimum at the earliest flag date 29.4). The J curve is flat across the region, so the choice within it costs little; the choice between it and 22d or 57d costs a lot (J 13.7 and 17.4 vs ~19.6-19.9).
identification_status.what_would_identify_it: ~9 months of history. With 270 days the threshold could be validated at a dozen flag dates each with a >150d lookback cap, and the drift would be measurable rather than confounded with left censoring.

addressable_population.where_the_missed_half_sits: All 28,986 missed churners have recency BELOW 42.2d at the flag date, by construction: median 23.7d, IQR [13.9, 34.6]. 36.1% sit in [30, 42.2) -- the band the naive 30-day rule would have caught, which is precisely the recall it buys and the false positives it pays for.
addressable_population.binding_rule_for_08_09: DO NOT treat the flagged population as the at-risk population. Sizing an intervention off 36,495 flagged users understates the at-risk base by 25,292 (41% short), while 3,694 of those flagged need no intervention. Any reach or ROI denominator built on the flagged count must be divided through by recall (53.09%), or it is wrong by roughly a factor of two.

base_rate_reconciliation.question: 03's Spec B gives a 56.9d forward window yet finds only 15.16% returning, against 02's D60 purchase retention of 21.08%. Is the 84.84% true-churn base rate fair?
base_rate_reconciliation.verdict: FAIR FOR THE QUESTION IT ANSWERS, and not comparable to 02's figure.
base_rate_reconciliation.anchor: 02 starts each user's clock at their own first order; 03 starts every user's clock on one calendar date. Return probability is a function of recency: the freshest stratum of 03's panel (recency <7d, i.e. 02's starting condition) returns at 27.42% over 56.9d, falling monotonically to 7.58% for the longest-lapsed band.
base_rate_reconciliation.composition: 02's population is a FLOW (new first-time buyers, all at recency 0); 03's is a STOCK (median recency 42.2d, only 4.73% within 7d of a purchase, 80.0% with one order). If the stock sat where 02's population starts, the churn base would be 72.58% rather than 84.84% -- the 12.26pp gap IS the recency mix.
base_rate_reconciliation.proof_of_agreement: Running 02's own first-order-anchored measure on 03's panel users reproduces 02 exactly: D30 14.08%, D60 21.08%. The notebooks do not disagree.
base_rate_reconciliation.left_censoring: Observable recency at F* is capped at 95.1d and users last active before 2019-10-01 are absent entirely, so the stock holds no long-dead customers. 84.84% therefore UNDER-states a mature retailer's point-in-time churn base.
base_rate_reconciliation.does_the_degeneracy_depend_on_it: NO, and this was the reason for checking. The cost model prefers flagging everyone once R exceeds the MAXIMUM LOCAL RETURN ODDS (0.378), not anything derived from the aggregate base rate; observed threshold 0.472 confirms the mechanism. On 02's own anchor the D60 odds are 0.267, still far below any realistic R, and reweighting the panel to 02's D60 rate moves the threshold only 0.472 -> 0.705. Section 3's argument is ANCHOR-INDEPENDENT and would not change if the base rate were 79%.

criteo_dataset.schema_note: f0-f11 dense float features (anonymised); treatment 1/0; visit, conversion, exposure binary outcomes. No user id and no timestamp -- one row per randomised user.

naive_ate_unvalidated.warning: Raw difference in means, computed here ONLY to confirm the file is usable. It is NOT a result: 07 must derive the ATE properly with SRM and covariate-balance checks, CIs, and ITT vs TOT (exposure is post-randomisation, so conditioning on it breaks randomisation).

criteo_dataset.verified_by: scripted check outside the notebooks, after 03. 07 owns all analysis of this file.
criteo_dataset.why_it_is_here: REES46 has no randomised experiment (principle 10). Criteo is the genuine one (principle 11) and is what lets 07 show that risk-targeting != uplift-targeting -- the argument 03's cost-model degeneracy already points at from the observational side.
